- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [30. Januar 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.92

- Datum: 30.1.1941

pages.transcription:
30. I 1941 Dear Hannah & Manfred,
from Lottes letter you will see, that we
are trying out all possibilities - boarding
school or private for Eva and I hope the de-
finitive choice will be the right one. Both
possibilities - private and boarding school -
have their advantages; be sure we will do
our best. But now I want to ask you a
favour. I would like very much that Man-
fred and you go to Bath immediately
he has passed his examinations in Febru-
ary. Like in Shakespeares Julius Cesar I
am afraid of the „ides of March“; it is
no secret and the newspapers are full
of it here, that the Huns will start the
long expected air attack and I believe
that Manfred should just after the streuous
days of his studies and examinations
have the necessary rest. As for the materi-
al side I tell you that I have to deliver
my last foreign investments on the
latest order, which included all kinds
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf einem Aerogramm-Formular. Die Tinte ist violett. Die Lesbarkeit ist gut.

pages.transcription:
and so my bank account will be con-
siderably increased, so that you can
dispose freely. Please follow my advice
- you know how I appreciate your courage
but I cannot approve that a man like
Manfred, instead of continuing his
scientific work in a relatively quiet
place, should be worn by a continuous
strain on his nerves. Had he any public
duty I would be the last to advise you
to take some rest but as his medical
practice has gone down he does best to
devote him entirely to the science and
perhaps to write in Bath some scienti-
fic essays. You cannot imagine how
much I feel all the sufferings in England,
the present ones and perhaps still more
the coming ones and our hope is that fi-
nally the States are speeding up; only
the public machinery is so slow and I
wish I could oil it a little. Please follow
my advice, I have seldom been mistaken
and I wish that a man like Manfred
should remain fit for his scientific work and his
future. Yours sincere Stefan
